lines: אוֹהֵב אוֹתְךָ, אוֹהֵב אוֹתְךָ, אוֹהֵב אוֹתְךָ
אָז אֶשָּׁאֵר חַיָּב לְךָ כָּל־עוֹד אֶחְיֶה
כִּי לְךָ אֲנִי, כִּי לְךָ אֲנִי, כִּי לְךָ אֲנִי
כִּי לְךָ אֲנִי, כִּי לְךָ אֲנִי, יֵשׁוּעַ
וְתֵן לִי מִמְּךָ חֶסֶד כָּל־יְמֵי חַיַּי

review: The hymn is the captive heart's triple confession: 1:1–6 is Song 4:9 (לִבַּבְתִּנִי) with Ps 45:12, 2:1–6 is Isa 53:4–5 with 1 Cor 6:20, and 3:1–6 is Rom 12:1 with 1 Pet 4:11.

The last two lines of each stanza are the same repeated acclamation (אוֹהֵב / כִּי לְךָ / לִכְבוֹדְךָ), and the payload keeps each stanza's pair verbatim, because the print repeats the phrase four times and then adds the name.

1:4 וְכָל־גִּיד וָגִיד בִּי יִפְעַם וְיֹאמַר — the Arabic كُلُّ عِرْقٍ فِيَّ يَنْبِضُ يَقُول is 'every vein in me pulses, saying'; biblical Hebrew has no vein-word, so the line uses גִּיד, the sinew of Gen 32:26 and Job 10:11, with the doubled distributive, so the whole frame of the body is speaking.
